newsitem.title: USA: Trichet can't rule out Russia in Paris Club in 97.
newsitem.headline: Trichet can't rule out Russia in Paris Club in 97.

text.p: Technical difficulties preventing Russia from joining the Paris Club of creditor states are likely to be resolved quickly and Russia could join the Paris Club this year, French officials said on Sunday.
"There are discussions under way. Some technical difficulties remain to be resolved. I think they are going to be resolved quickly," Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told a news conference.

Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet, asked about Russian Paris Club membership, said he did "not rule out" the possibility that membership could come this year. Trichet is a former chairman of the Paris club of official creditors.

Moscow, which has rescheduled the Paris Club debts it inherited from the former Soviet Union, wants to join the club as a creditor to increase the chance of paybacks from countries lent money by Moscow in Cold War days.

The loans, often denominated in now defunct convertible roubles, were extended to Soviet allies in the developing world more on grounds of political expediency than because Moscow expected to get the money back.
Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Sunday that Russia hoped to join the Paris Club by the end of 1997 and the World Trade Organization by the end of 1998.
